text:
Ryan Leonard is 21 and already one of Washington's most dangerous shooters. He has nine goals in 20 games, has scored in four straight, and six of his 16 points have come on the power play. His hardest shot this season, 93 mph, sits in the 96th percentile. It hasn't all been clean: the NHL fined him the maximum for a high stick on New Jersey's Cody Glass in mid-November, though he wasn't suspended.

How much of the scoring is real? Most of it. His own expected goals (the quality of his chances) are up sharply from last season, 1.33 per 60 minutes against 0.87. The finishing will likely cool: nine goals on 6.3 expected, shooting 17% after 13% last season.

The defensive side is the work in progress. At five on five Washington's share of chances is a little worse with him on than without him, and Evolving-Hockey flagged the same cost last season, along with a real gift for drawing penalties. For context, forwards drafted sixth to tenth since 2005 scored a median 0.40 points a game in their first full season. He's at 0.80.
headline: Ryan Leonard keeps finding the net
